On the Russia files he testified that he obtained documents and interviews from Soviet defence officials in the early 1990s and has 'now shared with this Task Force' - the printed hearing carries no statement that he shared them with BAASS or the DIA, which is why this is tier 2. It is an allegation by a named witness, not a documented transfer.

dossier.narrative:
The reason this node matters more than its size suggests is that the board can date the 1989 broadcasts only indirectly. The broadcasts themselves were not opened. What was opened is a Las Vegas Review-Journal report of 19 June 1990 which records, contemporaneously and for its own unrelated reasons, that Lazar had been the focal point of KLAS reporting. That is why `klas-lazar-broadcasts-1989` is built as a deliberately thin node anchored on a 1990 newspaper line with its air dates carried at Tier 3, rather than as a confident record of what aired and when.

That thinness is the honest state of the evidence and it should not be quietly improved. The station's own archive was not reached, and three attempts to open the successor site returned HTTP 403. A session that opens a 1989 artefact will be able to move several Tier 3 claims in this cluster to Tier 1 in a single stroke, and that is the highest-value gap in it.

The station's later role is separate and better documented. Knapp's reporting is one of the routes by which the AAWSAP contract and the Reid correspondence reached the public record, which is why this node carries edges to `aawsap`, `harry-reid` and `james-lacatski` alongside the Lazar ones. It is a newsroom that has been the first public custodian of this subject twice, thirty years apart.

dossier.whatItIs: KLAS-TV, the CBS affiliate on Channel 8 in Las Vegas, and the originating institution of the Bob Lazar claim. Its reporter and news anchor George Knapp, who joined in 1981, broadcast the programmes in May and November 1989 that put Lazar and the name S-4 into public circulation. A Las Vegas Review-Journal report of 19 June 1990 records contemporaneously that Lazar was the focal point of those broadcasts, which is how the board dates them without having opened the broadcasts themselves.
dossier.whyImplicated: A local television newsroom is on this map because the modern subject has a traceable point of origin and this is it. Almost everything the board carries downstream of 1989 about S-4, about element 115 and about a reverse-engineering programme at a Nevada site descends from a sequence of reports on one CBS affiliate. The station is not a commentator on this story. It is the custody point for the story's first public form, and the board treats it the way it treats any custodian: the institution that held and released a claim, distinct from the claim's truth.
